question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Cutting corners

options.text: To take the long way around
To do something quickly or cheaply, often at the expense of quality or safety

solution: The correct answer is** "To do something quickly or cheaply, often at the expense of quality or safety."** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **"Cutting corners"** means taking shortcuts or finding ways to do something faster or cheaper. (शॉर्टकट अपनाना या किसी काम को तेजी से या सस्ता करने के तरीके खोजना) • This phrase often implies that the shortcuts being taken may compromise quality or safety. • **Example**: *The construction company was **cutting corners**__ to finish the project on time.* • The correct answer is Option 2. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** • **Option 1, "To take the long way around,"** is the opposite of cutting corners and implies taking extra time or effort to do something. (कुछ करने में अतिरिक्त समय या प्रयास लगाना) • **Option 3, "To follow the rules strictly,"** is not related to cutting corners and is actually the opposite behavior. (नियमों का सख्ती से पालन करना ह) • **Option 4, "To be honest and fair,"** is also not related to cutting corners and refers to ethical behavior. (नैतिक आचरण) 2f:T4df, Here, the erroneous part is **"that angry."**
